description: EMBOSS 6.6.0 dotmatcher (600 DNA / protein pairs equal): the dot plot of two sequences by windowed substitution-matrix scores. On every diagonal a window of windowSize residue pairs slides along; a maximal run of windows whose summed matrix score reaches threshold is one segment from the first residue of its first window to the last residue of its last window. Returns the segments in the order the program draws them, 1-based inclusive positions on both sequences (the program's own scan treats the SECOND sequence as its first: the first diagonals start on the first residue of sequence2). matrix = BLOSUM62 | PAM250 | EDNAFULL | any EMBOSS matrix name; default EDNAFULL when sequence1 consists of nucleotide codes, EBLOSUM62 otherwise; a character that is not a letter of the matrix scores 0. A window may be as long as a sequence (the diagonals that fit are scored); a window LONGER than a sequence makes the program read its zero-filled buffer beyond the end (scored 0; segments may end beyond the sequence; only overhangs up to 8 residues are reproducible, further the program reads uninitialised memory and usually crashes; this port scores every position beyond the end 0); a window longer than the longer sequence gives no segment. A nucleic first sequence needs a nucleic second one (ArgumentException, the program's 'Sequence is not nucleic'); letters are read in either case; 720 edge rows (lower case, ambiguity codes, '*', gap characters, default matrix, window >= length) equal the program (A4-9). Input sequences are read as EMBOSS reads them (A4-3, one shared reader): only letters and '*' are kept; gap characters (- . ~ ?), '#', '+', '_', digits, blanks and every other character are dropped first, and positions, lengths and scores count the cleaned sequence (e.g. needle of AC-GTTAGC.TT* and ACGTTAGCTT: score 58, length 11, as the program). The plot is refused with an ArgumentException above 4 194 304 segments (SequenceAligner.DotMatcherMaxSegments; a threshold of 0 or less over a long pair): raise the threshold or the window.

sequence1.description: First sequence (the plot's y axis in the program).

threshold.description: Score a window must reach (dotmatcher -threshold, default 23).

matrix.description: Optional substitution matrix: any built-in matrix by EMBOSS or NCBI name - BLOSUM62, PAM250, EBLOSUM30 ... EBLOSUM90, EPAM10 ... EPAM500 (protein) or EDNAFULL, EDNAMAT, EDNASIMPLE, ENUC.4.4 (IUPAC DNA). When given, match/mismatch are ignored, residues are scored by the published table (any protein or IUPAC symbol of the matrix; case-insensitive) and gapOpen/gapExtend may be fractional (the EMBOSS needle/water models: gapOpen = -(G - E), gapExtend = -E for -gapopen G -gapextend E). The result then also carries the real-valued exactScore.

sequenceQualifiers.description: EMBOSS sequence-input qualifiers as on the command line, with the input number: -sbegin1 3 -send1 -2 -sreverse1 -slower1 -supper1 -scircular1 -snucleotide1 -sprotein1 and the same with 2 for the second sequence (begin / end: 1-based, negative = from the end; -sreverse: reverse-complement a nucleotide sequence, the range then refers to the original; -snucleotide / -sprotein force the type). Measured on EMBOSS 6.6.0: the alignment covers the range, and the formatted alignment (default format 'pair') reports the positions of the ORIGINAL sequence, counting down for a reversed one. Omit for the whole sequences. The text is resolved exactly as the EMBOSS program resolves it on its command line after the sequence arguments (ACD, 6.6.0): -sbegin1 3, -sbegin1=3, -nosreverse1, -sreverse1 N, any case, -/--/ prefix, and every UNIQUE abbreviation (-sbeg1, -sre2; uniqueness is decided among all qualifiers of the program, an ambiguous or unknown one is refused). The number is the sequence (1, and 2 for the second sequence of a two-sequence program; 1 for a program with one sequence). An unnumbered qualifier belongs to the LAST sequence given (-sbegin 3 is -sbegin2 3 in a two-sequence program) until a qualifier of another sequence ends that tie; after that it applies to all sequences. -sformat -sask -squick -sdbname -sid -iquery -ufo -fformat -fopenfile are accepted without effect (residue strings have no file); any other qualifier or a stray word is refused. dotmatcher scans the whole length over the cut text (-send has no effect except a NUL at the cut; -sbegin shifts the range to the front): the program's own behaviour.

segments.description: Segments `{ start1, start2, end1, end2 }` (1-based inclusive on both sequences) in the order the program draws them.

errors.message: Sequence cannot be null or empty

examples.name: Two similar DNA sequences with an insertion
